upset_review.day1_upset: 9z (HLTV #17, VRS 1543) 2-0 Aurora (HLTV #6, VRS 1716) on Day 1 — including a 13-1 Nuke. Pre-match market had 9z around 30% (see the repo's day-1 backtest, strategy/day1.html); only 4% of the HotSpawn crowd picked 9z at that capture.
upset_review.why_it_is_not_a_general_favorite-fade si: Three of the four Day-1 favorites also won (Falcons 2-0 NIP, Legacy 2-0 PARIVISION, FURIA 2-0 BETBOOM). One upset in four matches does not establish that favorites at TWC are mispriced.
upset_review.day2_update: 9z lost 1-2 to Falcons (took Mirage) and Aurora won 2-0 vs NIP (Cache 13-9, Dust2 13-7). The upset case is alive but not dominant; the market moved Aurora to ~66% for the decider, which already prices in the 9z result.
upset_review.leaderboard_logic: The contrarian-but-not-stupid rule (declared in twc-2026/method.html): take an underdog only when its market probability is >= 35% AND its HotSpawn crowd ownership is a small fraction of that probability AND at least two independent bookmakers confirm the line. 9z at 34.04% market / 14% ownership (2.4x) is just below the 35% floor after the Day-2 move — watchlist, not activated. The safe pick that maximizes expected match points on 7 offered points is Aurora.
